DISCUSSION ITEMS

The Board discussed the ongoing situation with CEI (Brent Beatty), who has not paid outstanding membership/vendor partner fees since August 2025 and has been unresponsive to recent communications. After extended discussion, the Board agreed that CEI has been given ample opportunity to respond and that no further outreach is needed at this time.

blocks.label: ACTION
blocks.text: S. Thomas to remove CEI's access to Circle.

The Board agreed that when vendor partner registration reopens in August, S. Thomas will send a general invitation, including a value proposition overview, to course-material vendors and publishers who are not current partners (including CEI), inviting them to apply or reapply for partnership for the 2026–27 year.

The Board discussed a potential partnership/sponsorship with Ambassador Education Solutions, including the broader question of what it means for CSC membership when an outside company manages some or all of a member's course materials or store operations, while the store itself remains institutionally owned and operated.
Key points raised:
Membership eligibility is tied to the store being institutionally owned and operated and staff being employed by the institution, with limited grandfathered exceptions.

The Board discussed restricting Circle access so that institution-employed staff retain full access (subject to appropriate discretion over what is shared with an outsourced partner), while outsourced-partner staff would have no access to Circle, and the course materials section could be disabled for non-institutional users. G. McPherson confirmed this is feasible.

The Board discussed concerns about data-sharing with companies that could use member data as leverage with senior institutional leadership, balanced against the recognition that member institutions can share their own data regardless of CSC's policies.

The Board agreed a member survey on this topic was not the right approach at this stage, given the potential for a mismatch between member sentiment and the Board's broader financial and strategic view.
The Board noted that Ambassador's outreach (through both S. Bell and S. Thomas) reflects broader industry trends already affecting several member institutions.

blocks.label: ACTION
blocks.text: S. Bell to invite Ambassador Education Solutions to present to the Board (rather than to individual member institutions) and to coordinate a date via a poll.

S. Thomas presented a proposed floor plan and booth map. Premium ("connected") booths, which include a full day of scheduled vendor meetings, are grouped together (31 booths); standard booths are located in a lower-cost area of the venue with easier loading-dock access. The plan is currently modelled on approximately 60 vendor partner booths. K. Stonehouse presented an alternative model (adjusting connected-booth pricing to $5,800 and increasing standard booths to 36 at $3,700) that would yield approximately 67 booths at similar or greater overall revenue. No final booth count or pricing was adopted; S. Thomas to continue refining the model.

S. Thomas noted the incremental cost of a course materials day is limited to per-person food and beverage costs (approximately $160/person), as no additional room space is required. The Board discussed whether course material vendors should be integrated into the main floor as standard booths or given a dedicated day/space with scheduled short presentations to publishers and vendors, to make participation more meaningful for that audience. No decision was reached; the format is still to be finalized as part of the broader course material strategy.
The Board discussed delegate, vendor, and sponsorship pricing for the 2027 conference:

Delegate registration: the Board discussed a full conference rate of $299 (a $25 reduction from last year) and leaned toward a simplified structure of a full-conference rate plus a single flat daily rate (approximately $199), rather than a fully itemized daily pricing model, to avoid overcomplicating registration. A reduced rate (approximately $100) for a half-day, non-member option on the final day was also discussed as a way to attract nearby institutions and help fill the floor.
Vendor partner fee: proposed reduction to $500 (from a higher prior amount), reflecting reduced administrative overhead, capped at one booth per company.

Exhibitor booth pricing: standard booths proposed at $4,500 (consistent with last year's pricing) and premium/connected booths at $6,500, plus a $10,000 sponsorship level (excluding booth). The Board discussed adding a lower-cost sponsorship option and moving away from traditional "gold/silver/bronze" tier naming, which has become associated with entrenched historical pricing expectations, while still providing accessible entry points with benefits proportional to sponsorship level.
The Board agreed pricing needs to be finalized by June 30, 2026, so that registration and website materials can move forward.

blocks.label: ACTION
blocks.text: S. Thomas to begin building out the registration/website structure based on the agreed pricing framework and bring finalized pricing back to the Board for review (via Circle) by June 30, 2026.

The Board remains on track for an estimated $20,000–$22,000 surplus at fiscal year-end. Board members were reminded to submit any outstanding expense reports.

I. May proposed postponing the "Course Materials – Back to Basics" style member session originally contemplated for this summer, given capacity constraints. The Board agreed to hold the session in August 2026, with I. May, K. Stonehouse, and S. Willis (and potentially S. Bell) completing preparation work in July.
The next Board meeting will be held on July 20, 2026.
